tldr: AI labs and governments both formalized external oversight of frontier AI claims this month. OpenAI stood up an outside advisory group to vet its own mathematics results, and DeepSeek is now being pulled directly into intergovernmental AI-risk discussions.
whats_new: DeepSeek is set to join a UN Security Council briefing on artificial intelligence risks, putting a Chinese frontier lab in a formal international risk-governance forum for the first time in this window.
why_it_matters: Formal review is arriving from two directions at once — labs self-policing benchmark claims and governments pulling labs into oversight forums — so expect more requests to substantiate claims with independent evidence, not just vendor numbers.

beats.headline: DeepSeek's frontier-lab profile is now common wire-photo shorthand for AI coverage
OpenAI forms an outside advisory group to vet its own math/AI results
DeepSeek to brief the UN Security Council on AI risks

open_questions: What specifically will DeepSeek present at the UN Security Council briefing, and will the briefing be made public?
Will OpenAI's advisory group publish independent findings, or only internal review notes?
Does either development lead to a concrete verification standard for frontier AI claims, or stay symbolic?
take_for_builders: If you cite frontier-lab benchmark or safety claims in your own evals, track how these advisory and governance bodies define verification standards — that's likely where audit requirements for vendor claims will originate.
